name: Summarize YouTube videos with GPT-4o-mini and email the brief via Gmail

parameters.content:
## 🧠 YouTube video to executive brief, in your inbox

### Who's it for
Researchers, newsletter writers and busy teams who get sent hour-long videos and need the substance in two minutes — a TL;DR, the key points, the quotes worth keeping, and whether it's worth a full watch.

### How it works
Drop a video URL into the Config node and run. A hosted Apify actor (called over plain HTTP) fetches the transcript — preferring human-made captions over auto-generated ones — then GPT-4o-mini turns it into a tight brief: TL;DR, five key points, notable quotes and a who-should-watch verdict. Gmail delivers the brief with the video title in the subject line. Videos that can't deliver a transcript fail with a clear, typed reason.

### Requirements
- An [Apify](https://apify.com) account + API token
- An OpenAI API key
- A Gmail account for sending

Transcript cost is [$0.002 per video](https://apify.com/beacondata/youtube-transcript-scraper) — videos without captions are never charged (the call also carries a $1 cost cap). The OpenAI call on a 12k-character excerpt costs well under a cent with GPT-4o-mini.

### How to customize
Swap the prompt for show-notes or social posts, batch multiple URLs, trigger it from a Telegram bot, or send the brief to Slack or Notion instead.

## 🛠 How to set up

1. **Create an Apify account** at [apify.com](https://apify.com) (takes a minute, card not required) and copy your API token from **Console → Settings → API & Integrations**.
2. **Create the credential:** in n8n choose **Create credential → Header Auth** and set
   - Name: `Authorization`
   - Value: `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN` (paste the token you copied in place of YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN)
   then select it on **Fetch the Transcript**.
3. **Open **Config**** and set your own values.
4. Add your **OpenAI** credential on the summarize node and your **Gmail** credential on the send node.
5. Run it once with the test button, check the output, then activate.

values.content: You turn video transcripts into executive briefs. Respond with simple HTML only: use h3 elements as section headings, ul/li lists for points, and blockquote elements for quotes. Do not use markdown. Do not include html, head or body wrapper elements. Sections, in order — TL;DR: 2-3 sentences. Key points: a list of exactly 5 items, each starting with its rough [mm:ss] timestamp taken from the markers in the excerpt. Notable quotes: 2-3 short verbatim quotes in blockquote elements, each with its rough timestamp. Who should watch: one honest sentence on who gets value (and who can skip it). Base everything strictly on the transcript excerpt; never invent content, names or numbers.
